**Anti-tamper kits.** Tamper-evident enclosures, lock upgrades, GPS tracking for mobile units, vibration alerting.

**Additional batteries.** Battery bank upgrades for sites with shading, high cellular draw, or extreme cold cycles.

**LPR add-on.** Retrofit LPR onto Swift Deploy and Solar Pole units. 95%+ accuracy, sub-3-second alerts.

**Signage.** Warning, surveillance, and trespass signage — printed, posted, and rated for outdoor multi-year exposure.

**K-rail and barrier mounts.** Mount cameras and lights to concrete K-rail without trenching or core drilling.

**Cellular and Starlink upgrades.** Backhaul redundancy and Starlink kits for remote sites.

h1: Boundary Guard Pro. 500+ feet of fence line, no blind spots.
heroSubhead: A single PTZ leaves gaps along long fence lines. Boundary Guard Pro is engineered for linear perimeters — 500+ feet of overlapping coverage from one solar-autonomous unit. From $1,800/mo.
body:
## Most trailers solve a point. This one solves a line.

A PTZ trailer is excellent at covering one location and useless at covering a 600ft fence line. Operators have to pan to a problem after motion is already in progress. By the time the camera is on the intruder, the intruder is at the fence.

Boundary Guard Pro is built around overlapping fixed sensors plus PTZ for verification. The whole fence is in frame the whole time. Motion triggers the right sensor; PTZ snaps to the event for high-detail capture and SOC verification.

## How the coverage works

- **Multi-sensor array** covers 500+ linear feet without gaps
- **Overlapping fields** mean intrusion at any point along the line triggers verified detection within seconds
- **PTZ verification** auto-cues to the alerted sensor
- **AI analytics** filter wildlife, weather, and vehicle pass-bys

## Power and form factor

- Solar-autonomous, multi-day battery reserve
- IP66 enclosure
- -20F to 120F operating range
- Dual-SIM cellular backhaul
- AI VisionStream integration standard
- ONVIF/RTSP compliant

## Pricing

- Lease: from **$1,800/mo** including AI VisionStream
- SOC monitoring optional, priced per unit
- Multi-unit and multi-month discounts available

## Where it earns its keep

Long construction fence lines. Material yards. Solar farm perimeters. Utility substations. Quarries. Logistics yards. Anywhere "we need to watch the whole fence, not just the gate" is the requirement.

A typical 1,000ft perimeter runs two Boundary Guard Pro units for full coverage. A 2,000ft perimeter runs three units staggered. We will scope it.

faq.q: Why not just put two Swift Deploy trailers along a fence?
faq.a: You can, and many customers do. Two Swift Deploy units cover the line but leave coverage gaps between them. Boundary Guard Pro covers the line continuously from a single unit, with PTZ verification on each event. Lower per-foot cost on long perimeters.

faq.q: Can I run Boundary Guard alongside Sky Guard MSU?
faq.a: Yes. Common pattern: Sky Guard on the high-value gate or yard with thermal and radar, Boundary Guard on the long fence runs. Both feed the same AI VisionStream and SOC.

faq.q: How is detection different from a typical PIR or motion sensor fence?
faq.a: Camera-based detection with AI classifiers means an alert comes with video evidence and is filtered for wildlife and vegetation. PIR fences alarm on everything; this alarms on what matters.

faq.q: Does the SOC monitor all 500 feet?
faq.a: Yes. Every alerted segment triggers an operator review with video. Live audio challenge through PA on the unit. 97% false alarm reduction.

finalCTABody: Send us your fence line length and threat profile. We will scope unit count and pricing in 24 hours.

h1: License Plate Recognition Cameras for Accurate Vehicle Identification
heroSubhead: A purpose-built LPR camera, the VDS platform, and SOC verification — packaged as one buyable system. 95%+ first-pass read accuracy at vehicle speeds up to 50 mph.
body:
License plate recognition cameras help commercial teams identify vehicles automatically, trigger alerts for plates of interest, and generate searchable reporting for investigations, access control, and operational oversight.

Unlike general surveillance cameras, LPR systems are only valuable when they produce two outcomes consistently: readable plate captures and a workflow that turns plate data into action.



## What License Plate Recognition Cameras Do

License Plate Recognition (LPR) is a surveillance capability that captures a vehicle’s license plate, converts the plate image into text, and makes that information usable for search, alerting, and reporting.

Organizations use LPR cameras to:

Log vehicles entering or exiting a location

Alert on watchlists (authorized vs unauthorized plates)

Support investigations with time-stamped evidence

Reduce manual gatehouse/security checks

Improve site accountability across multiple locations

When buyers search “LPR camera,” “license plate camera,” or “automatic license plate reader,” they’re typically trying to solve one of these problems:

“We need to know which vehicles are on-site and when”

“We need fast alerts for unauthorized or repeat offender vehicles”

“We need evidence we can retrieve quickly without reviewing hours of footage”



## How License Plate Recognition Works

A commercial LPR system usually follows a simple workflow:

Capture At A Predictable Point

The camera captures plates at entrances/exits or chokepoints where vehicle movement is consistent.

Optimize The Plate Image

Settings (exposure, shutter speed) and lighting determine whether the plate is readable.

Ocr Reads The Characters

Optical Character Recognition converts the plate image into searchable text.

Match Against Lists Or Filters

Plates can be checked against allow/deny lists, hotlists, or operational filters.

Trigger Alerts And Generate Reports

Alerts notify the right team; reports document the event with time, location, and associated video.



## What Data Can LPR Capture (and What It Can’t)

LPR is most valuable when expectations are clear. A properly configured deployment can capture reliable “plate events” that are searchable, reportable, and usable for alerts. But performance depends on placement, lighting, vehicle speed, and the platform package you deploy.



### What LPR Can Capture

Plate number (core output)

Plate image (evidence snapshot for verification)

Timestamp (date/time of the plate event)

Location context (site, lane/entry point, or camera name)

Camera/device ID (useful for multi-site reporting and audits)

Event history (searchable plate reads across time and locations)



### Alerts, Watchlists, and Operational Workflows

Watchlists (allowlist/denylist or “plates of interest”)

Real-time alerts when a watchlisted plate is detected

Search and reporting (full or partial plate searches, filters by date/time and location)

Evidence-ready exports (plate event + related images/clips, based on retention settings)



### Optional Vehicle Attributes

Direction of travel (in/out, lane direction)

Vehicle type/classification (e.g., car vs truck)

Make/model/color (available in some deployments depending on platform + analytics package; validate per configuration)



### What LPR Can’t Reliably Capture

Plates that aren’t visible (mud, damage, obstructions, plate covers, bike racks, trailers)

Consistent reads at extreme angles or long distances

Reliable reads in poor lighting without proper setup (headlight glare, backlighting, low-light corners)

High-speed reads in uncontrolled lanes without the right angle/settings

Driver identity (LPR identifies vehicles via plates, not people)

Perfect accuracy in every condition (read rate depends on environment and configuration)



### How to Improve Data Quality: Quick Requirements Checklist

Define the capture point (entrances/exits or chokepoints with predictable movement)

Control angles and distance (ensure the plate is large enough in-frame to read)

Design for night performance (plate readability, not just “a visible scene”)

Define what happens on a match (who gets alerted, escalation steps, reporting)

Confirm retention needs (how long plate events and related footage must be stored)



## LPR Camera Accuracy Requirements

If you want LPR to work in real conditions, this is the section that matters most. Most underperforming LPR deployments fail for predictable reasons: bad angles, uncontrolled lighting, or plates too small in frame.



### Placement and angle

LPR works best at chokepoints:

Entry and exit lanes

Gate approaches

Yard access points

Drive lanes that naturally slow vehicles

Why it matters: plates need to be large enough in-frame and captured at a usable angle. Wide “overview” placement is great for context, but it often fails for consistent plate capture.



### Vehicle speed and distance

Speed changes the capture requirements:

Faster vehicles need tighter placement and settings designed to reduce motion blur.

Longer capture distances make plates too small and reduce OCR reliability.

If you can control speed at entry points, LPR success rates typically improve significantly.



### Lighting and nighttime performance

Night is where LPR projects win or lose. Common failure modes include:

Headlight glare washing out plate detail

Underexposure in poorly lit lanes

High contrast scenes (bright fixtures + dark shadows)

LPR cameras often require purpose-built lighting and careful placement to preserve detail at night.

Camera settings (shutter and exposure)

Even high-end cameras can fail if settings are wrong:

Shutter too slow = motion blur

Exposure too bright = reflective plate washout

Exposure too dark = unreadable characters

For a more in-depth guide, explore the perfect setting guide for license plate recognition cameras.



## Where LPR Cameras Work Best

LPR produces the best ROI when vehicles must pass through predictable paths and when there’s a clear outcome tied to plate capture.



### Parking And Access Control

Use LPR to:

Log entry/exit events automatically

Alert on unauthorized plates

Support enforcement and dispute resolution

Reduce manual checks and friction at gates



### Logistics Yards And Warehouses

Use LPR to:

Track truck movements and timestamps

Verify deliveries and departures

Improve perimeter accountability

Support investigations after incidents



### Construction sites and temporary operations

Use LPR to:

Log vehicles entering and exiting job sites

Identify repeat unauthorized vehicles

Support incident timelines when theft occurs

Improve oversight across multiple projects

If you’re deploying security quickly on changing sites, LPR is commonly paired with mobile surveillance trailers.



### Municipal and Public Safety Applications

Use LPR for:

Vehicle-of-interest alerting

Corridor-based monitoring where fixed infrastructure exists

Evidence support for investigations and public safety initiatives



## Alerts, Watchlists, and Reporting Workflows

LPR becomes operationally valuable when alerts and reporting are defined.

A practical LPR workflow answers:

What triggers an alert (watchlist hit, time window, location rule)?

Who is notified (security, property manager, dispatch, law enforcement liaison)?

What is the escalation path (verify → notify → respond → report)?

What report is generated (plate, timestamp, camera/location, associated video)?

If you need verified response and standardized reporting across sites, LPR is often paired with remote video surveillance monitoring.



## LPR Deployment Options: Fixed, Mobile, or Hybri

Buyers typically choose one of three approaches:



### Fixed LPR installations

Best for:

Permanent facilities

Controlled entry/exit lanes

Stable lighting and infrastructure



### Mobile LPR deployments

Best for:

Temporary risk periods

Construction sites that change weekly

Locations without ready infrastructure

Fast deployment needs after incidents

Internal link: mobile surveillance trailers → /products/mobile-surveillance-trailers/



### Hybrid approach

Common in the field:

Use mobile deployments immediately for rapid coverage

Transition to fixed infrastructure once the site stabilizes

Keep workflows and reporting consistent across both



## What Affects Pricing and Scope

Pricing and scope depend on how you plan to use LPR. Key factors include:

Number of capture points (entrances, exits, chokepoints)

Vehicle speed and lane design (affects placement and settings)

Lighting requirements (night performance is a major driver)

Alerting and monitoring requirements (hours covered, escalation, reporting)

Data retention expectations (how long records must be stored)

Multi-site needs (standardization, permissions, centralized reporting)

Procurement model also matters. Many organizations compare:

Purchase (long-term ownership)

Lease (capex vs opex flexibility)

Rental (short-term or temporary risk periods)



## License Plate Recognition Camera FAQs

What is the difference between an LPR camera and an LPR system?

An LPR camera captures plate images. An LPR system includes the camera plus OCR software, searchable history, alerts/watchlists, and reporting workflows.

What affects license plate recognition accuracy the most?

Placement at chokepoints, vehicle speed, lighting (especially at night), and correct shutter/exposure settings are the biggest drivers of accuracy.

Can LPR work at night?

Yes, but nighttime performance depends on glare control, lighting design, and settings that preserve plate detail without washout.

Where should LPR cameras be installed for best results?

Entrances, exits, and lanes where vehicles slow down are the most reliable capture locations.

Can LPR trigger alerts for unauthorized vehicles?

Yes. Most commercial systems can run watchlists (authorized vs unauthorized plates) and generate alerts based on site rules.

Can LPR be deployed on mobile surveillance trailers?

Yes. LPR is commonly paired with rapid deployment platforms for construction sites, temporary risk periods, and locations without ready infrastructure.

MAKE THESE TESTIMONIALS SPECIFIC TO THE MOBILE SURVEILLANCE PRODUCT



## Protect Every Vehicle Entry—With Real-Time LPR Alerts.

Get an LPR solution that captures plates reliably at entrances and chokepoints, flags vehicles of interest, and creates searchable reports your team can act on—day or night.

faq.q: What's the difference between this page and /platform/lpr?
faq.a: This page is the buyable product — camera + license + SOC bundle. /platform/lpr describes the software capability for customers who want to add LPR onto an existing VDS deployment using already-installed cameras.

faq.q: Can I use my own cameras?
faq.a: Yes, but accuracy will be camera-dependent. We support LPR on any ONVIF Profile-S camera through the platform. If you want the 95%+ accuracy numbers, use the purpose-built LPR camera.

faq.q: How many lanes does a typical site need?
faq.a: One per direction of travel you want to capture. A two-way driveway is two lanes. A four-bay loading dock is typically two to four lanes depending on geometry.

faq.q: Does the system store driver images?
faq.a: The LPR camera captures the plate, not the driver. If you want driver capture, pair LPR with a standard overview camera; the platform correlates the two streams.

faq.q: Is there a public records / FOIA concern?
faq.a: For private commercial customers, plate data is private business data. For public-sector customers, plate data may be subject to state public records laws — we configure retention and access accordingly, and provide documentation for compliance review.

body:
Remote surveillance trailer solutions give teams fast, flexible site security coverage without waiting on permanent installation. If you need to deter theft, document incidents, and improve response on a temporary or changing site, a mobile surveillance trailer provides rapid deployment coverage paired with platform visibility and optional remote monitoring.



## What is a Remote Surveillance Trailer?

A remote surveillance trailer is a mobile, deployable security system designed to provide camera coverage where permanent infrastructure isn’t practical—or where speed matters most. It typically supports:

Fast site coverage without permanent installation

Operation across varying site conditions

Centralized access through a cloud platform

Optional monitoring and alert workflows depending on the deployment model



## Remote Surveillance Trailer vs Mobile Security Trailer

Buyers often use “mobile security trailer” and “remote surveillance trailer” interchangeably. In practice:

Remote surveillance trailer emphasizes access, visibility, and remote operations.

Mobile security trailer emphasizes deterrence and rapid deployment for site protection. If your risk is after-hours access, repeated theft, or temporary high exposure, a trailer solution is often the fastest path to meaningful coverage.



## Key Features of Our Mobile Surveillance Trailers



### Rapid Deployment for Temporary or Evolving Sites

Secure construction phases, parking lots, events, and incident response without waiting on permanent installs.



### Solar-powered with Battery Backup for Off-grid Coverage

Maintain continuous monitoring in remote locations and power-limited sites.



### 4G/5G Connectivity for Instant, Wireless Operation

Get video access and alerts without relying on site Wi-Fi—ideal for remote jobsites.



### Built-in Compatibility with VisionStream and AI Analytics

Centralize visibility, alerts, and reporting—then layer analytics to reduce noise and speed response.



### Modular Designs for Flexible Configurations

Choose camera packages and accessories based on your risk—scale from one site to multi-location coverage.



## Where Mobile Surveillance Trailers Work Best



### Construction Sites

Construction sites change weekly, and risk often spikes during early phases and after-hours. A trailer provides fast coverage for equipment, perimeters, and access points without slowing progress.

Best-fit outcomes:

Deter theft and unauthorized entry

Document incidents with usable evidence

Support site oversight across multiple projects



### Parking Lots and Shopping Centers

Parking lots are large, exposed environments where visibility and response matter. Trailers help cover drive lanes, entrances, and high-risk zones, especially during peak periods or elevated risk.

Best-fit outcomes:

Reduce vandalism and vehicle-related incidents

Improve visibility in low-coverage areas

Support retail and property operations with faster incident review

Move to the new page URL for parking lots



### Logistics Yards and Warehouses

Yards often have perimeter risk, vehicle movement, and high-value inventory. A trailer provides coverage where fixed coverage is incomplete or where additional deterrence is needed.

Best-fit outcomes:

Support perimeter coverage

Provide oversight for high-risk zones

Improve reporting and incident review workflows

*Fix typo in Warehousing



### Public Safety and Municipal Use

Temporary deployments are common during events, high-traffic periods, and public safety initiatives. A mobile solution can provide situational awareness without permanent buildout.

Best-fit outcomes:

Rapid coverage where temporary visibility is needed

Consistent recording and retrieval for incidents

Scalable deployment planning

*Fix typo in safety



## How Deployment Works

A trailer deployment should be planned around outcomes, not just “placing a camera.”

The Vision Detection Process:

Coverage plan: Define what must be seen (entrances, perimeters, high-value zones).

Site requirements: Confirm constraints (placement, power availability, connectivity needs).

Deployment and configuration: Align camera placement and platform access to your workflow.

Operations: Establish how incidents are reviewed, escalated, and documented.



## Remote Surveillance Monitoring

Surveillance becomes significantly more valuable when there’s a defined response workflow. Depending on your configuration, monitoring can include:

Alert triggers based on activity patterns and site rules

Verification and escalation paths

Reporting that supports accountability and follow-up

When monitoring is a priority, pair the trailer deployment with the Remote Video Monitoring platform.

Internal link: /products/remote-video-monitoring/ anchor “remote video monitoring”



## Why Choose Vision Detection Systems Mobile Surveillance Hardware

Vision Detection Systems hardware is built for environments where fixed systems fall short—rapidly changing sites, remote locations, and high-risk areas that require reliable visibility fast. Our mobile surveillance trailers are engineered for deployment readiness, consistent uptime, and seamless integration with platform monitoring and analytics.



### Proven Reliability in Demanding Environments

Built for outdoor sites and challenging conditions where uptime matters.



### Rapid Deployment with Minimal Setup

Fast placement and activation so you can secure the site sooner.



### Fully Autonomous Power and Connectivity

Solar and battery backup with cellular connectivity for off-grid operation.



### Backed by Expert Service and Monitoring

Support and monitoring options designed for operational readiness—not just equipment delivery.



## What Does a Remote Surveillance Trailer Cost? Buy vs Lease vs Rental

Pricing and scope depend on how you plan to use the trailer—and whether you want to purchase, lease, or rent as a deployment strategy. Key factors include:

Deployment duration (short-term, seasonal, long-term): Shorter deployments often favor rental; longer-term coverage may favor lease or purchase.

Coverage complexity (site size, entrances, perimeters, lighting conditions): Larger sites and more critical zones typically require more robust configurations and planning.

Camera package and configuration (wide coverage vs identification detail): The right package depends on whether your priority is deterrence, incident documentation, or response.

Monitoring requirements (hours covered, escalation process, reporting): 24/7 monitoring, after-hours response workflows, and reporting requirements materially affect scope.

Multi-site needs (standardization, user access, reporting structure): Multi-location programs benefit from consistent configurations, centralized access, and repeatable deployment processes.

If you share your site type, timeline, and preferred procurement path, we’ll recommend the right configuration and deployment approach.

## Remote Surveillance Trailer FAQs



### 1) What is a remote surveillance trailer?

A remote surveillance trailer is a mobile, deployable security system that provides camera coverage without permanent installation. It’s designed for rapid deployment on sites like construction projects, parking lots, and temporary risk areas, with centralized access through a cloud platform and optional remote video monitoring.



### 2) What’s the difference between a remote surveillance trailer and a mobile security trailer?

Most buyers use the terms interchangeably. “Remote surveillance trailer” typically emphasizes remote access, visibility, and platform monitoring, while “mobile security trailer” emphasizes deterrence and rapid deployment. In practice, both refer to the same category of deployable site security units—what matters is the configuration and monitoring workflow.



### 3) How quickly can a mobile surveillance trailer be deployed?

Deployment time depends on site conditions and coverage goals, but the process is designed for speed: confirm placement requirements, define the coverage plan (entrances/perimeters/high-value zones), deploy the unit, and configure access/alerts. If you have an urgent need (theft, vandalism, project delay), rapid deployment is often the primary reason to choose a trailer.



### 4) Do mobile surveillance trailers work in remote or off-grid locations?

Yes—remote and off-grid sites are a common use case. Many deployments use solar-powered and battery-backed configurations combined with cellular connectivity (4G/5G) to support operation where permanent power and wired internet aren’t available.



### 5) Can I monitor the trailer remotely, and what happens when activity is detected?

Yes. Remote monitoring can include live access to video feeds, alert triggers based on site rules, and escalation workflows. Depending on your setup, the workflow may include verification, notifications, and reporting for accountability and follow-up. For monitoring-specific details, link to: /products/remote-video-monitoring/.



### 6) How much does a remote surveillance trailer cost, and do you offer lease vs rental vs purchase?

Cost depends on deployment duration, site complexity (perimeter size, entrances, lighting), camera package/configuration, and monitoring requirements. Many buyers choose between purchase, lease, or rental based on timeline and budget structure.

### 7) Are mobile surveillance trailers a good fit for construction sites and parking lots?

Yes—construction sites and parking lots are two of the most common applications because they often need fast coverage, flexible placement, and reliable after-hours visibility. A trailer can cover access points, drive lanes, perimeters, and high-risk zones without slowing operations or waiting on permanent installs.



### 8) Can the trailer configuration be customized (cameras, coverage, upgrades)?

Configurations are often tailored to the environment and objective—wide-area deterrence, evidence capture, access-point coverage, or operational oversight. The right setup depends on what must be seen (faces, vehicles, entrances) and how you intend to respond when incidents occur.

body:
## Why thermal and radar belong on the same trailer.

Cameras lose people in shadow, weather, and dense vegetation. Thermal LWIR sees heat through all three. Radar sees motion through all three plus fog and rain. Run them together and you have detection that does not care what time it is or what the weather is doing. Run only one and you have a blind spot.

Sky Guard MSU is the only mobile unit in our catalog that ships with both, plus a 4K multi-sensor camera, LPR, and active deterrence — strobe and PA — on a single 22ft mast.

## Detection stack

**Thermal LWIR.** Detects body heat at long range in zero visible light. Trained AI classifiers on AI VisionStream filter wildlife and weather from human intrusion.

**Ground radar — 500ft.** Detects motion through fog, smoke, and heavy rain. Pairs with thermal for two-modality verification before an alert ever reaches an operator.

**4K multi-sensor camera.** Wide situational coverage plus tight PTZ-class detail on the same mast. Daylight evidence quality, full-color night vision via dual-spectrum optics.

**LPR.** 95%+ accuracy, sub-3-second alerts, immutable plate log feeding the same audit trail as your video.

**Active deterrence.** Multi-stage strobe and PA. SOC operators issue live voice challenges before law enforcement is dispatched. 97% of intrusions resolve at the audio challenge step — measured across our active fleet.

## Power and environmental

- **Solar.** 600W panel array, sized for full operation at 38N latitude with three consecutive overcast days
- **Battery.** 48+ hour reserve at full draw including thermal, radar, PTZ, illumination, and cellular
- **Enclosure.** IP66 — dust-tight, hose-down rated
- **Operating range.** -20F to 120F. Tested in Minnesota winters and Arizona summers
- **Mast.** 22ft, manual or hydraulic lift options
- **Backhaul.** Dual-SIM cellular standard. Starlink, point-to-point microwave, and hardline options on request

## Pricing

- Lease: from **$2,200/mo** including AI VisionStream
- Purchase: from **$38,000** plus monthly VMS and optional SOC
- SOC monitoring: priced per unit or per portfolio
- Most customers lease for projects under 24 months and purchase for permanent sites

## What ships with every unit

- AI VisionStream account, US-only AWS region
- 30/60/90-day cloud storage tier of your choice
- RBAC, MFA, immutable 12-month audit log
- ONVIF/RTSP integration with any existing fleet
- Delivery, siting, and commissioning
- Firmware updates over the air for the lease duration

## Where it earns its keep

Construction sites with high copper, fuel, or equipment exposure. Utility substations and yards. Critical infrastructure perimeters. Solar and storage farms. Cargo yards. Anywhere a thermal-only or PTZ-only unit would leave a detection gap and a 2 a.m. phone call.

## When a trailer is the wrong tool.

Trailers are designed to move. If a site is staying put for two years or more, the wheels and registration are dead weight. Fixed solar poles trade redeployability for a lower lifetime cost, a smaller footprint, and a permanent install that survives a hard winter without service calls.

## What's on the pole

- 4K or HD camera options
- Optional PTZ
- AI analytics on edge plus cloud
- Optional LPR
- Solar array sized to site latitude and shading conditions
- Battery reserve sized for local weather conditions
- Cellular backhaul standard; hardline available

## Where they earn their keep

Permanent yards. Long-term construction parks. Solar farms. Substations. Storage facilities. Municipal lots. Schools and campuses. Any site where the trailer registration would expire before the project ends.

## How they connect to the platform

Same AI VisionStream account as your trailers. Same SOC. Same audit log. Mix fixed and mobile across a portfolio without managing two vendors.

## Pricing

Configured per site. Most fixed pole deployments price lower per year than equivalent trailer leases when the engagement runs 24+ months.

faq.q: Do you handle the install?
faq.a: Yes. Pole, foundation, solar, camera, and commissioning. We coordinate with your GC or municipality on permits.

faq.q: Can I move a fixed pole later?
faq.a: Yes, but the cost-benefit usually favors a trailer for sites that move. We will steer you to the right product for your timeline.

faq.q: What about lightning?
faq.a: Surge protection and proper grounding are part of every install. Standard for outdoor solar electrical work.

faq.q: Will the solar run cameras through a Northeast winter?
faq.a: Yes. Array sizing accounts for local irradiance and shading. Battery reserves are spec'd for multi-day overcast conditions in your specific geography.

## Built for crews who do not have 90 minutes to babysit a deployment.

Most "rapid-deploy" trailers in our category require two people, leveling jacks, mast guy-wires, and a separate cellular commissioning step. Swift Deploy was redesigned in 2023 around a single-operator workflow. Drop legs, raise mast, power on. The cellular link self-registers. AI VisionStream sees the unit before the operator gets back in the truck.

That redesign is why this is the most-deployed unit in our fleet across 30+ states.

## What's on the mast

**HD PTZ camera, 30x optical zoom.** Reads a face at 300ft and a plate at 200ft. Pan-tilt-zoom controllable from any device on AI VisionStream.

**Dual-spectrum imaging.** Full-color night vision without infrared illuminators that announce the unit's presence. Pairs visible and low-light sensors so footage stays usable from dusk through dawn.

**AI analytics.** On-edge person and vehicle detection. Cloud classifiers filter out wildlife, weather, and vegetation movement so operators only see real events.

**Optional LPR.** 95%+ accuracy, sub-3-second plate alerts, immutable log.

**Strobe and PA.** Active deterrence with SOC-triggered live voice challenge.

## Power and form factor

- **Mast.** 20ft, single-operator manual lift
- **Solar.** 400W panel array
- **Battery.** 36+ hour reserve at full draw
- **Enclosure.** IP66
- **Operating range.** -20F to 120F
- **Backhaul.** Dual-SIM cellular standard; Starlink and external antenna options
- **Detection range.** 300ft

## The deployment claim, broken down

"Under 20 minutes, one person, no tools" is the spec. Here is what that looks like in field time:

- 0:00 — arrive on site, position trailer
- 2:00 — drop stabilizer legs
- 5:00 — raise mast
- 8:00 — power on, cellular handshake
- 12:00 — first live frame in AI VisionStream
- 18:00 — operator confirms scene, adjusts PTZ presets

That is the median across our last 200 deployments. We have field data.

## Pricing

- Lease: from **$1,500/mo** including AI VisionStream
- SOC monitoring: priced per unit or per portfolio
- Multi-unit and multi-month discounts available
- Month-to-month after initial term — no 36-month lock-ins

## When to choose Swift Deploy over Sky Guard MSU

Pick Swift Deploy when your sites are well-lit at night, your perimeter is under 300ft, and your primary threat is human intrusion captured by a PTZ camera. Pick Sky Guard MSU when you need thermal, radar, and active deterrence on the same unit, or when sites lose visibility to weather or terrain.

## Where it earns its keep

Construction sites of all sizes. Equipment yards. Retail parking lots after hours. Cargo staging. Event security. Pop-up retail. Hospitality overflow lots. Anywhere "we need eyes on this by tomorrow" gets said in a meeting.
